mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative investor sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals strong economic activity, leading to positive investor sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% within a month, coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000, signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive investor sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.3% in 1 month AND PAYEMS rises > 200,000
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity and lower borrowing costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decrease and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which is a key driver of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increase and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
